Article Title: At 12, she was eve-teased, it changed her life; 24 years later, Suchika Tariyal is India’s first Asian Games MMA medallist
Article Text:
Suchika Tariyal

From self-defence to a life in combat sports

Suchika Tariyal (@suchika_tariyal Instagram)

Second Asian Games, different story

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: At 12, an incident of eve-teasing changed the course of Suchika Tariyal’s life.What began as a need to protect herself eventually became a journey through judo, Ju-Jitsu and mixed martial arts. And on Sunday, the 36-year-old Rohtak native broke new ground for Indian MMA at the Asian Games In the process, she became the country’s first athlete to secure an Asian Games medal in MMA, which is making its debut at the Games.The decision to take up judo after the eve-teasing incident was never meant to lead to a career on the international stage. But Tariyal steadily turned herself into one of India’s most versatile combat athletes.She began with judo before moving to Ju-Jitsu and eventually MMA in 2017. Her judo career brought eight national titles and international success, including gold at the 2019 Commonwealth Judo Championships and the 2019 South Asian Games. She also won silver at the 2018 Commonwealth Judo Championships and competed at multiple Asian championships.At the 2022 Commonwealth Games in Birmingham, she competed in the women’s -57kg category and narrowly missed a medal.Her transition to Ju-Jitsu produced another major achievement when she won gold in the adults Ju-Jitsu Contact Female -63kg category at the 2024 JJIF Ju-Jitsu World Championships.Tariyal made her MMA debut with a victory in 2017 but took a seven-year break from the sport while continuing her judo and Ju-Jitsu career.She returned to professional MMA in December 2024 after signing with BRAVE Combat Federation and won at BRAVE CF 92 in Bahrain.“Judo set me up for MMA, which for me is the ultimate level of combat sports. Because of judo, I was skilful in ground fighting and grappling. I only had to learn the standing game and striking skills for MMA. Switching from judo was not difficult. MMA is a test of all-round skills, and one has to be a complete combat athlete,” she said.The Aichi-Nagoya Games represent a second chance for Tariyal. At Hangzhou in 2022, she competed in kurash, but the campaign did not produce the result she wanted.“Life has given me a second chance at the Asian Games. In Hangzhou, it did not go the way I wanted because kurash was not popular in India and my preparation was not adequate. This time, I am fully prepared for MMA,” Suchika told SAI Media.Supported by the sports ministry’s Target Asian Games Group (TAGG) scheme, she entered Aichi-Nagoya after winning back-to-back bronze medals at the Asian MMA Championships in January and May this year.Her rise has also made her a familiar face beyond the combat-sports arena. She has more than 300,000 Instagram followers and has featured on MTV Roadies and Prime Video’s India’s Ultimate Warrior. She has also been honoured by the President and Prime Minister for her international achievements and contribution to women’s empowerment.But for Tariyal, perhaps the biggest purpose of her journey is what it can mean to young women.“I really want to inspire young women to take up MMA. I will be very happy even if one girl looks at me and says, ‘If Suchika can, I can too.’ In modern times, women need to defend themselves, and parents must let their children take up combat sports. MMA gives you that complete package. And women have a strong mindset to play combat sports. They can bear pain and can be more focused. If a woman can bear the pain of childbirth, MMA is nothing,” she said.Now, with an Asian Games medal already assured, Tariyal is keeping her focus on the competition rather than the achievement.She admitted, “There will be no easy fights. I am not thinking of results now. I don’t want to put myself under the pressure of expectation. I just want to give my 100% for India. For any fighter, a medal is the ultimate achievement, and I am no different."
Article Summary: Suchika Tariyal became India's first Asian Games medalist in mixed martial arts. The 36-year-old took up judo after an incident of eve-teasing aged 12. She has won eight national titles and won gold at the 2019 Commonwealth Judo Championships.

Article Text:
Deepika scores eight as India thrash Uzbekistan 19-0 in women's hockey opener

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

India's women's hockey team began their Asian Games campaign in emphatic fashion, cruising to a 19-0 win over Uzbekistan in their opening Pool B match here on Sunday.The contest was expected to be heavily one-sided and India lived up to those expectations from the opening whistle, repeatedly breaching an Uzbekistan defence that struggled to cope with the intensity and quality of the Indian attacks. Deepika was the star of the show, scoring eight times in a remarkable individual performance. She found the net in the 8th, 22nd, 25th, 33rd, 36th, 38th, 41st and 54th minutes to lead India's goal fest.Lalremsiami opened the scoring in the seventh minute with a close-range field goal before Deepika added India's second a minute later. Ishika then extended the lead in the 11th minute with a superb first-time finish from the left side of the circle after being set up by Sunelita Toppo.Baljeet Kaur made it 4-0 in the 12th minute, while Neha added another field goal six minutes later.Deepika then took centre stage again, converting a penalty corner with a powerful dragflick into the bottom-right corner. Navneet Kaur followed with a field goal before Deepika struck once more from a penalty corner to send India into half-time with an 8-0 advantage.The onslaught continued after the break, with India adding 11 more goals across the final two quarters.Alongside Deepika's eight, Ishika scored three times, while Lalremsiami, Baljeet, Neha, Navneet Kaur, Lalthantluangi and Sakshi Rana also got on the scoresheet.Ishika struck in the 42nd and 54th minutes after her first-half goal, Navneet added another in the 45th, while Lalthantluangi scored in the 43rd and 51st minutes. Sakshi Rana also found the net in the 43rd minute.The gulf between the two teams was also reflected in the possession and attacking pressure, with Uzbekistan struggling to retain the ball for sustained periods.The match also marked a milestone for veteran India goalkeeper Savita Punia, who earned her 320th international cap. With that appearance, she joined Vandana Katariya as the joint-most capped Indian women's hockey player.Savita had little involvement in the contest, however, as Uzbekistan rarely managed to create meaningful pressure and spent much of the match trying to contain India's relentless attacks.India, the second-highest-ranked side in the competition, will next face Indonesia on Monday.
Article Summary: Deepika scores eight as India thrash Uzbekistan 19-0 in women's hockey opener. Lalremsiami, Baljeet, Neha, Navneet Kaur, Lalthantluangi and Sakshi Rana also got on the scoresheet.

Article Title: Suchika Tariyal scripts history, assures India of first Asian Games medal in MMA debut
Article Text:
Suchika Tariyal assured India’s first medal at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games by reaching the women’s traditional 60kg MMA semifinal after defeating Mongolia’s Altanchimeg Baigalmaa.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

India's Suchika Tariyal secured the country's first medal at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games after defeating Mongolia's Altanchimeg Baigalmaa 2-0 in the women's Traditional Mixed Martial Arts 60kg quarterfinal on Sunday.The 36-year-old produced a composed performance to book her place in the semifinals, where she will compete on Monday. With both losing semifinalists guaranteed bronze medals, Tariyal's progression into the last four ensures India will return from the event with a medal.The achievement is particularly significant as MMA is making its Asian Games debut at Aichi-Nagoya 2026.Tariyal's latest success adds another chapter to an unusual combat sports journey that has taken her across several disciplines. She represented India in judo at the 2022 Commonwealth Games before competing in kurash at the 2023 Asian Games. In 2024, she also became a Jiu-Jitsu world champion.Having stepped away from competitive sport, Tariyal eventually returned after encouragement from friends. She opted to take up MMA and began another chapter in her career, overcoming several challenges along the way, including a knee injury, to earn her place in India's Asian Games contingent.Her quarterfinal against Baigalmaa saw Tariyal maintain control as she secured a 2-0 victory. The Mongolian, ranked 92nd in the Eurasia region, was unable to prevent the experienced Indian from advancing to the semifinals.Tariyal will now have an opportunity to add to her medal tally when she takes the mat again on Monday. Regardless of the outcome in the semifinals, her run has already delivered India its first medal of the Aichi-Nagoya Games.For a competitor who has moved between judo, kurash, jiu-jitsu and MMA, the medal is another milestone in a career defined by transitions across combat sports. Her Asian Games debut in MMA has now guaranteed her a place on the podium.
Article Summary: India's Suchika Tariyal secured the country's first medal at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games after defeating Mongolia's Altanchimeg Baigalmaa 2-0 in the women's Traditional Mixed Martial Arts 60kg quarterfinal. Article Title: Asian Games debut beckons for Deepu Mallesh after years of crowdfunded climbing
Article Text:
Deepu Mallesh

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

CHENNAI: For speed climber Deepu Mallesh, getting to the starting line has sometimes been as difficult as getting to the top of the climbing wall. From 2019-24, the 28-year-old relied on crowdfunding for most of his competitions. But financial constraints never stopped the Karnataka lad from pushing forward.He repeatedly lowered his own national record, with his latest mark coming at the Asian Championships earlier this year, where he clocked 5.39 seconds. The next stop in his journey is Japan, where he will make his maiden Asian Games appearance.“Competing in the Asian Games will help me on the path to Olympic qualification. Last year, the entire preparation was focused on making it to the Asian Games. I want to go below my national record and be a good competitor to others without putting pressure on me,” Deepu, who is also an online instructor, told TOI.While Deepu’s parents wanted him to study, he chose climbing as an escape route and tried the sport following his coach Shiva’s recommendation. The sport being included in the Olympics back then was a major push for Deepu to stay on.“Most of my competitions were crowdfunded with the help of my climbing community and others.The 2023 season was very difficult. To qualify for the Paris Olympics, I had to compete in six World Cups to improve my rankings and at least get to compete in Olympic qualifiers. But I could only participate in three WCs due to fund shortage and visa issues. Crowdfunding is always very risky. Until the very end, you will not know how much money you are going to get, how much you are going to spend, how much you have to work with.I could not plan things properly, but somehow, I tried to manage with whatever I had,” Deepu, who lowered the NR from 6.22s to 5.39s over the last few years, added.Just as the 2023 season was important for Deepu, next year will be equally crucial, with him having to compete in all the WCs and earn ranking points. But without sponsorship, he is unsure about the way forward after Asiad
Article Summary: Deepu Mallesh will make his maiden Asian Games appearance in Japan. The 28-year- old relied on crowdfunding for most of his competitions from 2019-24. He repeatedly lowered his own national record, with his latest mark coming at the Asian Championships earlier this year.

Article Title: Arsenal lose Premier League top spot after Brighton shocker, Raphinha shines for Barcelona
Article Text:
Arsenal's Bukayo Saka in action between Brighton's Olivier Boscagli, left, and Maxim De Cuyper during the English Premier League. (AP Photo/Kin Cheung)

Raphinha powers Barcelona

Inter fight back in Italy as Dortmund go top in Germany

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Arsenal lost top spot in the Premier League after suffering their first defeat of the season, going down 3-0 to Brighton. The Seagulls climbed to third after a strong week that also included a League Cup win over Manchester United.Arsenal dropped behind Manchester City on goal difference, with City able to move three points clear if they beat Sunderland on Sunday.Tottenham finally found the net but still lost 3-2 at home to Aston Villa, the reigning Europa League champions. Newcastle beat Hull City 2-1, Everton edged Ipswich 1-0, while Coventry ended a four-game losing run by beating Nottingham Forest 1-0.Barcelona continued its excellent start to the La Liga season with a 3-1 win away at Sevilla, making it seven league victories in a row. Raphinha was the star, scoring a hat-trick, with Lamine Yamal setting up two of his goals.Raphinha has now scored 12 league goals, already just one short of the 13 he managed throughout the whole of last season. Barcelona has scored 31 goals in seven games and moved six points clear of Real Madrid, which faces Atletico Madrid on Sunday.Sevilla took the lead through Youssouf Fofana, but Raphinha equalized midway through the first half after cutting inside and finding the bottom-right corner.Yamal then used his quick footwork to beat the Sevilla defense before crossing for Raphinha to head home in the 52nd minute. The young winger later assisted again for Raphinha's third.Elsewhere in Spain, Rayo Vallecano striker Sergio Camello scored his seventh goal of the season in a 1-1 draw at Osasuna. Racing Santander, who had lost 7-2 to Barcelona in midweek, suffered another heavy defeat, going down 5-0 to Celta Vigo. Pablo Duran scored twice. Athletic Bilbao and Alaves played out a goalless Basque derby.Inter Milan came from two goals behind to draw 2-2 with Roma in a clash between two unbeaten sides. Roma midfielder Manu Koné scored twice in the first half, but Lautaro Martinez struck twice after the break to rescue a point for Inter.Koné opened the scoring in the sixth minute after Nahuel Molina headed Paulo Dybala's cross back toward him. He scored again in the 37th minute after being set up by Gianluca Mancini. The goal was initially ruled offside but was awarded following a video review.Roma coach Gian Piero Gasperini had stopped Koné from being sold to Inter during the offseason. Martinez pulled one back soon after halftime and completed the comeback in the 79th minute.Lazio beat Venezia 2-0, while Cagliari continued its strong start with a 1-0 win over Udinese. Daniel Maldini, son of former Italy defender Paolo Maldini, scored for Cagliari. Bologna drew 1-1 with Torino after recently dismissing coach Domenico Tedesco.In German Bundesliga, Borussia Dortmund moved to the top of the table with a fourth straight victory, beating Stuttgart 1-0 through Maximilian Beier's goal.Dortmund now has a two-point lead over defending champion Bayern Munich.Borussia Moenchengladbach's coaching change failed to stop its poor run as the team lost 4-3 at home to Mainz for a fourth straight defeat, conceding 16 goals during the run. Freiburg drew 2-2 with Eintracht Frankfurt after twice coming from behind and remained level on points with Bayern. Werder Bremen and Hamburg also secured home victories.In France, Ghana striker Ernest Nuamah scored twice as Lyon defeated Rennes 4-0. Paris FC remained unbeaten after beating Strasbourg 2-1, with Ilan Kebbal and Pablo Pagis scoring. Coach Liam Rosenior faced his former club after leaving Strasbourg for a brief spell at Chelsea earlier this year.
Article Summary: Barcelona continues its excellent start to the La Liga season with a 3-1 win away at Sevilla. Raphinha was the star, scoring a hat-trick, with Lamine Yamal setting up two of his goals. Arsenal lost top spot in the Premier League after suffering their first defeat of the season, going down 3-0 to Brighton. Borussia Dortmund moved to the top of the table with a fourth straight victory, beating Stuttgart 1-0.

Article Title: Panama name 14 World Cuppers for India friendly
Article Text:
Panama were placed in a challenging World Cup group

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Panaji: At 44, Panama is the lowest-ranked team that India will face during the FIFA international match window, but Khalid Jamil’s team has a fierce battle on its hand as Los Canaleros will arrive here with 14 players who were part of the squad for the FIFA World Cup 2026.Panama were placed in a challenging World Cup group, which included England, Croatia and Ghana. Central America’s only representatives were competitive but suffered narrow losses against Croatia and Ghana, and ended their campaign with a 2-0 loss against England as Jude Bellingham and Harry Kane clinched top spot for the Three Lions.After ending without a point at the World Cup, coach Thomas Christiansen has now started rebuilding the squad. The former Spain forward has named a strong 27-member squad for the Asia tour with a mix of World Cup players, six debutants and two from the local league, Liga Panamena de Futbol: goalkeeper Marcos De Leon (Sporting San Miguelito) and midfielder Daivis Murillo (CD Plaza Amador).The players are expected to arrive in three batches, from 15 different countries. The coaching staff, support staff, and Panama-based players departed for India on Saturday night, and will reach Bengaluru on Monday, after a layover in Amsterdam.Panama will face India at the Sree Kanteerava Stadium in Bengaluru on Sept 25 before they travel to Japan to take part in the Kirin Cup, where they will join hosts Japan (world no. 17), Ecuador (25) and New Zealand (86).“The match against India will provide us with more opportunities to see the new players,” Christiansen said while announcing the squad. “We have a fair idea of what to do during these three games. We know, more or less, who will feature in these matches. This is a generational shift (for Panama), but in the end, we also want to compete and give a good impression of ourselves.”Panama has a fine mix of players who play across the world. Jose Cordoba dons colours for Norwich City in the EFL Championship (England’s second tier), while Carlos Harvey represents Minnesota United in MLS. Amir Murillo (Besiktas, Turkey), Andres Andrade (LASK Linz, Austria), and Jose Rodríguez (FC Juárez, Mexico) are the other notable players.“We have players who we have not yet seen (for the national team) and these games will help us evaluate them. We cannot throw all of them into the mix straightway. It will hamper their chances of proving themselves and showing us the quality they have,” said Christiansen, who etched his name into Panamanian football folklore by leading Los Canaleros to their second FIFA World Cup.BoxPanama World Cuppers for Asia tour: Orlando Mosquera, Cesar Blackman, Jorge Gutierrez, Amir Murillo, Andres Andrade, Jose Cordoba, Jiovany Ramos, Adalberto Carrasquilla, Carlos Harvey, Cristian Martinez, Jose Luis Rodriguez, Azarias Londono, Tomas Rodriguez, Jose Fajardo
Article Summary: At 44, Panama is the lowest-ranked team that India will face during the FIFA international match window. Los Canaleros will arrive here with 14 players who were part of the squad for the FIFA World Cup 2026. The players are expected to arrive in three batches, from 15 different countries. Panama will face India at the Sree Kanteerava Stadium in Bengaluru.

Article Title: 10-man Mohun Bagan clinch CFL title after final-day drama
Article Text:
Image credit: X

KOLKATA: Mohun Bagan SG clinched the CFL Premier Division title after a gap of 8 years, scraping past fellow challengers Mohammedan SC 3-2 in a dramatic final-day action at Barasat stadium on Saturday.Sahal Abdul Samad put Bagan in front in the 26th minute but Mohammedan SC finished the first half on level terms after Lalremsanga’s goal in the 42th minute. Bagan then suffered a blow to their ambitions when their goalkeeper Deeprobhat Ghosh was red-carded on the hour mark and Mohammedan SC captain Mahitosh Roy converted the resultant penalty to make it 2-1.Playing with 10 men for than half an hour, Sahal gave Bagan a semblance of hopes with his second goal in the 70th minute and Sayan Banerjee came off the bench to strike four minutes later to clinch the championship for Bastab Roy’s brigade.In a dramatic final day when as many as five teams of the Super 6 stage harbour hopes of winning the trophy, defending champions East Bengal FC demolished Coal India SPA 7-0 to finish second while the match between other two contenders Bhawanipore FC and United SC ended in a goalless stalemate.Bagan finished the championship round with seven points from 3 matches, ahead of East Bengal (5), Mohammedan SC (4) and Bhawanipore (4).On the judgment day, Mohun Bagan and Mohammedan SC entered the contest with four points each and faced a winner-takes-it-all situation. Bastab started his line-up with seven first-team players, including handing Lallianzuala Chhangte a debut in the CFL and showing their desperation for regaining the local league. Yet Deeprobhat’s act of madness when he felled Lalremsanga inside the box as the Mohammedan SC forward tried to get past him, inviting a straight red-card from referee Pratik Mondal and allowing the rivals to go ahead.By that time, news of East Bengal scoring their fifth goal at their home ground — a pre-requite for the red-and-gold side to pip other challengers had both matches at Barasat and Barrackpore ended in draws — reached the Bagan camp.Bastab was forced to rejig his line-up, taking off Chhangte and bringing in second-choice goalkeeper Syed Zahid Hussain and replacing Kiyan Nassiri with Sayan.The move eventually paid off as Sayan — who had contributed immensely to East Bengal’s march to the title last year — settled the nerves and the championship for his new team with a smart finish.At home, East Bengal ended up scripting the biggest margin of victory with goals from Akash Hemram (2), Bijay Murmu (2), Mohammad Bilal (2), Tanmay Das (66 penalty) and Uttam Hansda (90+8). But it was enough for them to deny Bagan their CFL title No. 31.
Article Summary: Mohun Bagan SG clinch the CFL Premier Division title after a gap of 8 years. Bagan scrape past fellow challengers Mohammedan SC 3-2 in a dramatic final-day action. Defending champions East Bengal FC demolished Coal India SPA 7-0 to finish second.

Article Title: 'Todos somos caballas': Why Kylian Mbappe is under fire from far-right groups in Spain over a t-shirt
Article Text:
LaLiga - Elche v Real Madrid - Estadio Manuel Martinez Valero, Elche, Spain - September 15, 2026. Real Madrid's Kylian Mbappe rolls up his t-shirt displaying a slogan in solidarity with the people of Ceuta

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Real Madrid forward Kylian Mbappe has come under criticism from conservative and far-right politicians in Spain and France after he did not fully wear a t-shirt supporting residents of Ceuta, Spain's North African territory that is dealing with a migration crisis.Immigration has become one of the biggest political issues in Spain in recent months after a large number of migrants entered Ceuta in July. The debate has also reached football ahead of next year's parliamentary elections.The controversy began before Real Madrid's LaLiga match against Elche on Tuesday. Mbappe, Vinicius Junior and fellow French player Ibrahima Konate partially rolled up t-shirts carrying the message "We are all Ceutans", which was meant to show support for people living in Ceuta, a Spanish territory bordering Morocco.Pictures of the three players quickly spread on social media and drew political reactions.A spokesperson for Spain's opposition Popular Party (PP) said she felt "deep shame" over the incident, while a lawmaker from the far-right Vox party said Spaniards were "perfectly free to feel outraged by three millionaires who live in Spain and then do not support Spaniards".Ultras Sur, a Real Madrid supporters' group linked to the far right and banned from the Santiago Bernabéu, called the players' actions "unacceptable" and demanded public apologies.The incident comes after more than 70,000 migrants crossed into Ceuta from Morocco on July 30 and 31 in a large influx that left scores dead and triggered disagreement within the European Union over immigration.Most migrants returned within hours, but thousands remained in difficult conditions in the city, staying in temporary shelters and makeshift camps. The situation has led to protests by local residents, some of which have been supported by far-right groups.Responding to the criticism, Mbappe said he stood with the people of Ceuta while also remembering migrants who lost their lives."I was in complete solidarity with Ceuta and all the victims.""But I also wanted to make a gesture and express my thoughts for all the immigrants who have lost their lives and who are also living in difficult conditions," he told sports daily AS.Real Madrid also defended its players' right to make their own decision over wearing the t-shirts.Before the match, both Real Madrid and Elche players came out wearing shirts with the slogan "Todos somos caballas" ("We are all mackerels"), with caballas being a nickname for people from Ceuta.Mbappe and Vinicius rolled up their shirts so the message was not visible before removing them as they left the tunnel, while Konate held his shirt in his hands.A Real Madrid official was quoted as saying Reuters that the club agreed to Elche's request to show solidarity with Ceuta but respected different opinions within the squad and allowed each player to decide whether or not to wear the shirt.
Article Summary: Kylian Mbappe comes under criticism for not fully wearing t-shirt supporting residents of Ceuta. Real Madrid players Vinicius Junior and Ibrahima Konate partially rolled up t-shirts carrying the message "We are all Ceutans" The shirts were meant to show support for people living in Ceuta, a Spanish territory bordering Morocco.

KOLKATA: East Bengal FC look to keep the early-season momentum going as Antonio Lopez Habas’s team begins its AFC Champions League Two campaign against reigning Jordanian champions Al Hussein in Amman on Wednesday.Last month, East Bengal qualified for the revamped second tier of Asian club football by brushing aside Kuwait’s Al Arabi SC and followed it with their Durand Cup triumph with another dominating performance against arch-rivals Mohun Bagan SG.“We are excited to participate in the ACL Two group stage. It's a unique chance to compete at the highest level in Asia, and we want to inculcate the same mindset in the players. We want to continue the winning momentum that we’ve achieved over the past two months. We want to replicate that success in the game against Al-Hussein,” Habas said during a press conference in Amman on Tuesday.The reigning Indian champions landed in Jordan with only three foreigners — Dani Ramirez, Mohammed Rashid and Croatian newcomer Diego Zivulic, but Habas kept his faith in the domestic firepower. Article Title: ‘Thank You, Colombia’: Captain James Rodríguez, 35, announces retirement from international football after extraordinary 15-year career
Article Text:
FILE - Colombia's James Rodriguez celebrates after defeating Costa Rica at the end of a friendly soccer match in Bogota, Colombia, Monday, June 1, 2026. (AP Photo/Fernando Vergara, File)

From a winning debut to Colombia's record cap holder

The captaincy, the tears and one more World Cup

Why James Rodríguez decided to walk away

35

Rodríguez's club career continues in Colombia

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

For 15 years, James Rodríguez was one of the first names that came to mind whenever Colombia walked onto a football pitch. The No. 10 shirt became closely associated with him, as did the captain’s armband, the spectacular goals and the expectations that followed him through three World Cups. On Tuesday, Rodríguez announced his international retirement in an emotional video, telling Colombian fans that it was time to close “one of the most important chapters” of his life. After 131 appearances for his country, the legendary No. 10 has brought that chapter to an end.Rodríguez's international story began in October 2011, when he made his Colombia debut against Bolivia and immediately announced himself by scoring the winning goal.He was only beginning what would become a 15-year relationship with the national team, eventually playing at the 2014, 2018 and 2026 World Cups. Colombia did not qualify for the 2022 tournament in Qatar, meaning Rodríguez's international career ultimately spanned three editions of football's biggest competition despite the four-year absence. He is tied with Carlos Valderrama and Freddy Rincon for the most tournament appearances by a Colombian.The tournament that defined his reputation, however, came in Brazil in 2014.Rodríguez scored six goals in five matches to win the World Cup Golden Boot, including the extraordinary volley against Uruguay in the last 16 that became one of the defining goals of the tournament and later won the FIFA Puskás Award.Colombia reached the quarter-finals before losing to hosts Brazil, but Rodríguez's performances had already changed the trajectory of his career. After the tournament, he earned his move from Monaco to Real Madrid, where he would play alongside some of the biggest names in world football.For Colombia, meanwhile, the No. 10 had become much more than a shirt number.Rodríguez eventually took on the responsibility of captaining his country as well, carrying the armband during a period in which Colombia remained one of South America's strongest sides.He finished his international career as Colombia's record cap holder, level with Carlos Valderrama and Freddy Rincón for the most tournament appearances by a Colombian, while his final figures stood at 131 appearances, 31 goals and 43 assists.Rodríguez's relationship with Colombia was never defined solely by the highlights.In his retirement message, he acknowledged the difficult periods alongside the celebrations and explained what representing the national team had meant to him throughout his career.“Today, I want to talk to you from the heart,” James said on social media on Tuesday. “After many years, many games and joys, and difficult moments, it's time to close one of the most important chapters in my life: my journey with the Colombian national team.”He described the responsibility attached to the shirt in equally personal terms.“Wearing this shirt was a dream, but also a huge responsibility,” James added. “Every time I entered a court, I understood that he didn't play just for me. I played for my family, teammates, thousands of Colombians who dreamed of all of us.“I had the honor of wearing the No. 10 shirt and also the captain's armband. I always tried to do it with respect, responsibility and understanding what it meant to represent Colombia. I had good days and very difficult ones, but I never stopped feeling proud of these colors.”His final appearance came on July 7, when Colombia faced Switzerland in the last 16 of the 2026 World Cup.The match finished 0-0 after extra time, before Switzerland won the penalty shootout 4-3, bringing Rodríguez's fourth and final World Cup campaign to an end.It also meant his last match for Colombia ended without the fairytale finish that might have suited the player who had given the country one of its most memorable individual World Cup performances.There had been another significant chapter two years earlier.Rodríguez captained Colombia to the 2024 Copa América final, where Argentina won 1-0 after extra time. It was Colombia's first appearance in the Copa América title match in 23 years, although Rodríguez ultimately finished his international career without a senior international trophy.His announcement was direct, with Rodríguez making clear that his decision was not about distancing himself from Colombia but about bringing an important period of his life to a natural conclusion.The caption accompanying his retirement video said: “Thank you for every match, every joy, every tear and every dream we shared. Defending the colours of the Colombia national team was one of the greatest honours of my life.”He ended the message with the same sense of gratitude.“I'm leaving calmly because I gave everything. Thank you for every moment, thank you Colombia,” Rodríguez said.Rodríguez is now, and while his international career is finished, he has made clear that he is not finished with football.Just last week, Rodríguez joined Atlético Nacional on a contract running through next June after leaving Minnesota United.The move takes him back to Colombian football for the first time since his teenage years at Envigado, where his professional career began, and gives the veteran midfielder an opportunity to continue playing in his home country after closing the door on international football.Atlético Nacional becomes the 14th club of a career that has taken Rodríguez through some of the biggest teams in Europe and North America, including Real Madrid, Bayern Munich and Everton.His club honours include two Champions League titles and two LaLiga crowns, while his international career produced the Golden Boot at the 2014 World Cup, 31 goals, 43 assists and more appearances for Colombia than any other player.There will be no more World Cup nights in the yellow shirt, no further Copa América campaigns and no additional occasions for Rodríguez to walk out wearing Colombia's No. 10 or captain's armband.For a generation of Colombian supporters, those two symbols had become inseparable from the same player.Now Rodríguez will try to write the final pages of his playing career at Atlético Nacional, while the Colombia team begins the task of imagining its midfield and its No. 10 shirt without the player who occupied both for so long.
Article Summary: James Rodríguez announced his retirement from international football on Tuesday. The No. 10 made 131 appearances for Colombia, including three World Cups. He is tied with Carlos Valderrama and Freddy Rincon for the most tournament appearances by a Colombian. He won the World Cup Golden Boot in Brazil in 2014.

Article Title: 'Nightmare!' Ronaldo suffers his worst Al-Nassr defeat to date as AFC Champions League Elite comeback ends in 4-0 humiliation
Article Text:
Ronaldo and Al-Nassr suffer a shocking 4-0 defeat on their long-awaited AFC Champions League Elite return/ Image: X

Al-Nassr suffer nightmare start against Al-Ain

Ronaldo suffers heaviest Al-Nassr defeat

Al-Nassr fans turn on Ronaldo and Postecoglou

Al-Nassr's return to the AFC Champions League Elite was supposed to offer an early glimpse of what the new season could bring. Instead, Cristiano Ronaldo and his teammates walked away from their opening night with a result that few inside the club would have expected, as Ange Postecoglou's side suffered a heavy defeat in the United Arab Emirates.Cristiano Ronaldo started for Al-Nassr, but there was little the captain could do to prevent a disastrous evening as Al-Ain swept aside the Saudi side 4-0 in their first AFC Champions League Elite match of the campaign.The defeat came in Matchday 1 of the newly formatted competition, meaning Al-Nassr's Asian campaign has barely begun, but the manner of the loss immediately puts Postecoglou's team under pressure.Al-Ain took control in the 25th minute, when Houssine Rahimi opened the scoring. Al-Nassr were unable to find a response before Rahimi struck again in the 63rd minute, leaving the visitors with a huge task just to get back into the match.Instead, the collapse continued.Soufiane Rahimi added a third in the 72nd minute, before Georgios Giakoumakis completed the rout five minutes from full-time to seal a stunning 4-0 victory for the UAE side.For all of Al-Nassr's possession, there was remarkably little attacking threat to show for it. Postecoglou's team controlled 58 per cent of possession and won the corner count 10-2, yet managed only three shots on target.Al-Ain, by comparison, registered seven shots on target and made their opportunities count.The result also extends an impressive start to the season for Al-Ain, who arrived unbeaten in their first five UAE Pro League matches, having recorded four wins and one draw.For Ronaldo, the scale of the defeat makes it particularly difficult to dismiss as an ordinary bad night.It is now the heaviest defeat of his Al-Nassr career since he joined the Saudi club in January 2023. His previous worst results in Saudi colours had both ended in three-goal defeats, with Al-Nassr losing 3-0 to Al-Hilal in the Saudi Pro League in December 2023 and 4-1 to the same opponents in the Saudi Super Cup in August 2024.The 4-0 defeat to Al-Ain is therefore a new low in terms of the margin of defeat during Ronaldo's time in Saudi Arabia It does not, however, match the heaviest losses of his entire career. Ronaldo's two worst defeats by goal difference remain Manchester United's 5-0 loss to Liverpool in October 2021 and Real Madrid's 5-0 defeat to Barcelona in November 2010, both five-goal margins.What makes Tuesday's result particularly damaging is when it arrived.Al-Nassr had only just returned to the AFC Champions League Elite after a one-year gap, with a new coach, a new season and renewed expectations surrounding a squad built to compete for major honours.The opening match was supposed to begin that campaign.Instead, Al-Nassr now sit at the bottom of the tournament standings after one match, having conceded four goals without scoring.The new AFC Champions League Elite format gives Al-Nassr some room to recover because this is no longer a traditional four-team group containing six matches.Instead, the competition now features a single league stage in which each team plays eight matches against eight different opponents.That means Al-Nassr have seven matchdays remaining, giving Ronaldo and his teammates plenty of opportunities to climb the table after their disastrous opening.Their next opportunity comes on October 12, when Al-Nassr host FK Neftchi Fergana.The scale of the response will matter as much as the result itself. A one-year absence from the competition had created anticipation around Al-Nassr's return, while Postecoglou had arrived with the task of turning a squad containing Ronaldo and other high-profile additions into a side capable of making a serious continental run.Instead, the first night exposed just how far there is still to go.The reaction from the stands was predictably furious after Al-Nassr were beaten at the Hazza bin Zayed Stadium.Supporters had expected something very different from the club's return to Asia's elite competition, particularly with Ronaldo leading the side and Postecoglou now in charge.Some fans directed their anger towards Ronaldo himself, with the captain's performance described by supporters as “pitiful” amid Al-Nassr's failure to seriously threaten Al-Ain for long periods.Postecoglou faced even sharper criticism.Supporters questioned whether the Australian had made the difference they expected after his appointment, with Al-Nassr appearing short of answers at both ends of the pitch as the scoreline continued to worsen.Calls for his dismissal grew louder as the defeat unfolded.For a club that entered its AFC Champions League Elite return with ambitions of going deep into the competition, there could hardly have been a more damaging opening night. Ronaldo and Al-Nassr now have seven matches to change the story, but the first one has already left them with a four-goal deficit and very little margin for another collapse.
Article Summary: Al-Nassr lost 4-0 to Al-Ain in their first AFC Champions League Elite match. The result leaves the Saudi side bottom of the group after one match. Al-NASSr have seven matches remaining to try and make up for the loss.
